variant: Mooney M30 '301' proof-of-concept prototype N301MX (one built, Experimental category, first flight April 1983, Kerrville TX)

span.note: 36 ft 9 in per Air International Jan 1984 'Airdata File' pp.50-51 (cited by Wikipedia; not seen first-hand). MAOE newsletter (https://mooneyevents.com/Mooney301.html) gives 37 ft; Wikipedia prose also says 37.0 ft vs 36.42 ft for M20. Treat as 36.75-37.0 ft.

area.note: 150.0 sq ft per Air International Jan 1984 via Wikipedia (secondary). Implied AR ~9.0 with 36.75 ft span; wing loading 26.7 lb/ft2 at 4000 lb.

wing.airfoil: NASA NLF(1)-0315 natural-laminar-flow section root to tip (Selig/Lednicer 'Incomplete Guide to Airfoil Usage' https://m-selig.ae.illinois.edu/ads/aircraft.html; Wikipedia citing airfoils.com). Jane's 1983-84 (via Wikipedia infobox) calls it 'Mooney 0315'. High-aspect-ratio tapered planform, double-slotted Fowler flaps over ~90% of trailing-edge span, upper-surface spoilers plus small stub/'feeler' ailerons with anti-servo tabs (AOPA Pilot June 1983 https://www.aeroresourcesinc.com/uploads/198306-1983%20Mooney%20301%20Prototype.pdf).

tc_root.note: From airfoil designation NLF(1)-0315 (15% t/c); secondary compilation, not a Mooney drawing.

tc_tip.note: Same section root to tip per compilation.

canard_or_htail.airfoil: Inverted cambered section ('basically an upside-down wing'), one-piece all-moving stabilator, per Mooney engineering test pilot Bob Kromer (https://themooneyflyer.com/issues/2012-OctTMF.pdf). NOTE conflict: Wikipedia says fixed horizontal stabilizer with trim-tab elevators; Kromer's first-hand account is preferred for the prototype as flown 1983-84.

vtail.note: Aft-swept fin (unlike M20's forward-raked fin) per Wikipedia; no dimensions found.

length.note: 29 ft 9.25 in per Air International Jan 1984 via Wikipedia; MAOE gives 29 ft 8 in.

fuselage.note: Overall height 9 ft 10.75 in (Air International via Wikipedia; MAOE 9 ft 10 in). Pressurized 5.0 psi (8,000-9,000 ft cabin at 25,000 ft). Six seats club arrangement, center aisle, aft air-stair door, wraparound windshield; flush/butted skins, recessed windows (AOPA Pilot June 1983).

cooling: air-cooled; low-set engine with deliberately very small cooling inlets and exhaust exits (LoPresti low-drag cowl) per AOPA Pilot June 1983 and Wikipedia; single large AiResearch turbocharger with intercooler; cowl flaps not documented

diameter.note: 6 ft 6 in, per Jane's 1983-84 pp.444-445 as cited in Wikipedia infobox (not seen first-hand).

engine.model: Lycoming TIO-540 (turbocharged, intercooled; some sources write TSIO-540); exact dash number not found

hp.note: 360 hp rating stated in AOPA Pilot June 1983; Kromer: '360 takeoff horsepower'

mtow.note: Design gross 4,000 lb (MAOE; Plane & Pilot; Air International via Wikipedia)

empty.note: Air International Jan 1984 via Wikipedia. MAOE useful load 1,600 lb implies 2,400 lb target empty; new owners judged it ~200 lb over target (Ball 1998 via Wikipedia).

fuel_usable.note: 100 US gal capacity (MAOE, Jane's via Wikipedia); usable split not stated

perf_points.note: Bob Kromer (Mooney engineering test pilot 1983-86) speed/power tests: 'probably a 235-240 KTAS airplane at 75% power at 15,000-20,000 feet, using 18 gallons per hour'. Midpoints shown; weight not given. Flown 1984 after ownership change.
Factory/projected: cruise 75% power at max altitude 235 kt, 19.7 gph (MAOE newsletter). Altitude read as 25,000 ft max operating altitude. Design claim, not measured.
Projected top speed 262 kt / 301 mph (name origin); altitude assumed 25,000 ft ceiling. Plane & Pilot and Wikipedia say the prototype was slower than expected.
Jane's 1983-84 cruise 259 mph (225 kt) via Wikipedia; altitude/power not given in secondary source.
Controlled flight at 56 KCAS (Kromer); Jane's lists 64 mph (56 kt) flaps-down stall.

ntsb_total.note: CAROL query Aircraft.AircraftModel contains '301'/'M30' with make Mooney returned no Mooney 301/M30 records (see note in gaps). Prototype only; Experimental; ~70 h in 1983 plus Socata data flights late 1984.

safety.pattern: RECORD: no accidents or incidents found. Test pilot Kromer (first-hand) reports a serious, non-certifiable pitch-control deficiency: with rapid control inputs in gusty air on approach, pitch authority became 'almost non-existent', as if the tail were in dead air. Flight Test attributed it to the inverted-airfoil one-piece stabilator; he recommended replacing it with a conventional fixed stabilizer and elevator, which was never done. INFERENCE: this is a fixable configuration issue (conventional tail), not a fundamental flaw; but any revival must treat tail design as unvalidated. No fleet means no statistical record.
notable: 1983-1984 - Kerrville TX - no damage - pitch-control deficiency in gusty-air approaches identified in flight test (Kromer, The Mooney Flyer Oct 2012, https://themooneyflyer.com/issues/2012-OctTMF.pdf); no NTSB record

why_died_detail: Program started 1980 (announced June 1980), delayed ~2 years by Republic Steel's reluctance to invest (AOPA Pilot Jan 1983 https://www.aopa.org/news-and-media/all-news/1983/january/pilot/the-high-and-the-mighty). Flew April 1983 (first flight ~7 Apr per MAOE; first public flight 21 Apr per AOPA Pilot June 1983) as a company 'homebuilt' proof-of-concept, ~70 h. July 1984 LTV bought Republic Steel and divested Mooney; new French-led owners (Couvelaire, with Armand Rivard) judged it ~200 lb overweight and too slow (they wanted ~300 kt) and redirected effort to a turboprop with Socata (TBM 700). Prototype also had an unresolved pitch-control problem (Kromer). Piston-single pressurized market was also collapsing in mid-1980s product-liability era. A revival with modern turbo/intercooling would need: conventional tail, weight reduction, and a market that now has the M350/M600/Malibu and TBM above it.
rights_hints: Mooney engineering data and the prototype went to Socata (Aerospatiale) at Tarbes in 1987 under the TBM International JV (formed June 1987, Mooney + Aerospatiale); Socata test pilots flew the 301 for drag/performance data from late 1984 (Kromer). Mooney withdrew from the JV in May 1991, leaving TBM to Socata (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SOCATA_TBM). Daher took 70% of Socata in 2009, 100% in 2014; name became Daher 2015. Prototype returned to Kerrville, wings removed, airframe donated/scrapped via an A&P school in Abilene TX (MAOE; Wikipedia 'citation needed'). Registration N301MX now on an unrelated Aviat Husky. INFERENCE: original M30 drawings may sit with Mooney International (current Mooney owner) or Daher archives; no public statement of who holds them was found.
